description: Job Highlight Drive high-quality infrastructure delivery by providing technical expertise, supervising works, and ensuring compliance with design and safety standards. About The Project Office Gazanche Primary School is located in Gurage Zone, Central Ethiopia Region, about 28 km south of Wolkite Town, serving three rural kebeles with an estimated population of around 10,000 people. Established in 2010 through community efforts, the school currently accommodates about 1,000 primary students (Grades 1–8) and 50 nursery children. However, the existing infrastructure is inadequate and below national standards, consisting mainly of traditional wooden-mud classroom blocks with only nine classrooms, resulting in severe overcrowding with up to 80 students per classroom. The school also lacks basic facilities such as an administration building, library, reliable sanitation, electricity, water supply, and secure fencing. Existing latrines are temporary and structurally unsafe, while most buildings are deteriorated and unsuitable for a safe learning environment. Planned Improvements The project intends to establish a new primary school infrastructure that will provide a safe, inclusive, and climate-resilient learning environment. Planned works include the construction of new classrooms, administration and library buildings, gender-separated sanitation facilities, fencing, walkways, drainage systems, landscaping, and solar power installations. These interventions aim to reduce overcrowding, improve safety and sanitation, and expand access to quality education, particularly for girls, children with disabilities, and underserved rural communities, in line with SDG 4 (Quality Education) and Ethiopia’s Education Sector Development Programme VI. Role of the Civil Engineer The Civil Engineer will be based in Gazanche and serve as the site supervisor and technical focal point for the construction works. The role involves ensuring that all activities are implemented in accordance with approved designs, technical specifications, quality standards, and project schedules. title: Donor Assistant (South West)
description: Home About us Our people Join our team Donor Assistant (South West) Donor Assistant (South West) Part time (Minimum of 12 sessions a year) | Saturdays and Sundays| £13.45/hour Gloucester, Bristol, Cardiff, Wellington, Wells The Role Award-winning animal charity, Pet Blood Bank UK, is recruiting for a Donor Assistant to work at venues across the South-West. As part of the collection team, this role involves working at donation sessions where lifesaving blood is collected from dogs. As a Donor Assistant, you are responsible for helping to run the session, including holding our donors while they give blood, tidying and resetting the donation room for the next donor, running blood tests, assisting with paperwork and the potential to meet up to 23 potential donors and their owners at each session. The role is key to ensuring successful donation sessions and providing a positive experience for all our donors and their owners. As part of our charitable remit, our aim is to advance animal health and welfare and to relieve suffering by providing quick and convenient access to blood. Every unit of blood helps save up to four other lives, saving thousands of lives every year. Our values Caring. Pioneering. Real. These are the values Pet Blood Bank UK is built upon. Our values bind us together as a charity and guide everything we do. We expect every team member to know, understand and embody our values, helping to build our reputation as a pioneering, caring and practical charity. Read more about our values. What you’ll do Assist the Veterinary Surgeon and Veterinary Nurse with all donors to ensure health check, donation and post donation tasks are carried out. Assist with paperwork and running blood tests. Help to hold our donors during the donation process. Assist with monitoring donors throughout the donation process. Build a rapport with donors and their owners to ensure they feel valued and involved - provide a positive donation experience from start to finish. Maintain a good relationship with our host venues. Communicate with Pet Blood Bank staff, including your regional collection team, Regional Coordinator, Area Supervisor and office staff. Attend events to promote Pet Blood Bank and recruit donors and volunteers What we need We’re Looking For Someone Who Is An excellent communicator with strong customer care skills. A team player. Experienced in animal care, ideally with a qualification but not essential, and have a love of working with dogs. This is an ideal role for a student/newly qualified veterinary nurse/student vet/person with animal experience. Organised and proactive. Availability on Saturdays and Sundays Holds a full UK driving licence and has access to their own transport. To ensure you can complete the required training we may arrange for you to attend some sessions outside of the region, mileage allowance and accommodation will be organised where required. What’s in it for you In return, we offer full training and a great team working environment. The rate of pay is £13.45/hour and a mileage allowance of 35p/mile offered for travel to and from venues. Further details Sessions are approximately 8 hours in length and flexibility is essential as start and finish times will be dependent upon the travel time to and from the venues. Donor Assistants are expected to work at least one session per month to meet the required expectation of a minimum of 12 sessions a year to maintain their skills, but additional sessions may be available. Own transport is required to get to venues - please note not all venues are accessible by public transport. Before applying, please read our Guidance for Candidates. title: Site Supervisor
description: Department: Building Fabric - Delivery Employment Type: Full Time Location: South West Reporting To: Stephanie Chapman Compensation: £38 - £45 / year Description Harmony is on a mission to be the best life safety partner to work with and for. Rated an ‘Outstanding Employer’ by Best Companies in 2025, we are only getting bigger and stronger — and we’re looking for A-players to help us get there. We are passionate about making a difference and obsessed with quality. Our goal is to build a world where every resident can sleep safely at night, knowing their home is 100% safe. We have an opportunity for a Site Supervisor to join our Projects team. You will oversee the delivery of works on site, holding your team and subcontractors to Harmony’s standards and ensuring every project is delivered safely, compliantly and to the highest quality. This is more than just a site role. It is about bringing the right energy, accountability and resilience to our mission of saving lives through fire and height safety. Key Responsibilities Quality and Compliance Management — ensure all works are completed to Harmony and BM TRADA standards. Carry out timely checking of works on site and ensure accurate data input throughout. Site Management — oversee site set-up and sign-off, stock management, delivery of prelims, pre-condition surveys and post-inspections to allow for final sign-off by the Project Manager. Identify and flag variation opportunities immediately. People Management — resolve day-to-day issues, boost team morale, manage conflict and identify resource requirements. Maximise the productivity and utilisation of colleagues and subcontractors on site. Quality Control — ensure all works are certifiable and compliant, delivered to both client and Harmony expectations. Carry out regular spot checks and record findings accurately. Client Management — attend pre-start meetings and ensure the site is always tidy and representative of Harmony’s brand. Communication — provide regular progress updates to the Project Manager and weekly reports to the client. Attend calls as needed and agree reporting frequency with the Project Manager. Health and Safety — implement Harmony’s H&S policy across all sites. Induct new trades, ensure completion of all H&S paperwork, deliver regular toolbox talks and maintain a safe working environment at all times. Skills, Knowledge & Expertise An A-player mindset — high standards, extreme ownership and the drive to do things properly, the first time. Experience running a project to time and on budget. A strong problem solver who perseveres until the job is done. Ability to develop good working relationships with clients, subcontractors and colleagues. Proactive, confident, tenacious, resilient and flexible. An ambassador for Harmony’s values and behaviours on every site. Comfortable working flexibly across sites, with a willingness to travel as required. Full UK driving licence. Job Benefits This is a chance to run live sites for one of the UK’s fastest-growing life safety specialists — the kind of work where you can see what you’ve delivered at the end of every week and know it makes residents safer. At Harmony, we ask a lot — and we give a lot back. The hours are real, the standards are high and the work is demanding, but for those who show up, deliver and go the extra mile, the rewards follow. A-players here enjoy a competitive salary, a Personal Development Plan with ongoing training and coaching, unlimited holiday, a bonus scheme paying up to 50% of annual salary, enhanced maternity and paternity, lunch, snacks and refreshments on us every day at the office (fresh fruit and Takeaway Fridays included), a team social budget, cycle to work, an auto-enrolment pension, two major company events a year and our Reward and Recognition scheme — including European mini-breaks for those who go above and beyond. It is a collaborative, high-energy environment focused on doing things the right way — technically, practically and safely — and none of it is a perk for showing up; it’s what we share with the people pulling the business forward. Harmony is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all applicants for employment regardless of age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief. We want everyone who works with us to feel valued and to make a difference.

title: Country Manager
description: 【岗位背景】 星星充电作为全球大型智能充电设备供应商及微电网系统先驱，已于2026年初开启IPO进程。根据公司全球化战略，我们正全力拓展非洲、中东、东南亚等高增长市场。本岗位将作为公司在非洲目标国家的“一 把手”，负责从0到1搭建本地业务体系，推动充电桩、微电网、户用及工商业储能、光伏安装项目的规模化落地。 【岗位职责】 1. 战略制定与业务落地 市场洞察与战略规划： 根据非洲目标国家（摩洛哥、南非、尼日利亚、卢旺达）的市场特点，制定中短期业务战略。重点结合当地脆弱的电网现状及“Mission 300”等国际能源接入计划，识别高价值落地场景。 业绩指标负责： 对目标国家的销售与营收目标负责，重点突破“光储柴”微电网、矿区离网储能、工商业“储能+充电”一体化项目。 2. 市场开发与生态构建 客户与渠道拓展： 挖掘高耗能矿企、大型工商业园区、电信基站及当地能源投资商等核心客户；发展与当地工程施工商（EPC）的长期伙伴关系，监管项目履约质量。 政府与金融关系： 维护与当地能源部、电力监管局、投资促进署的关系，确保项目合规；对接国际金融机构（如世界银行、非洲开发银行）及本地银行，探索适合非洲市场的融资解决方案（如PPA模式、租赁模式）。 3. 解决方案与交付协同 商务技术支持： 深入掌握微电网及储能商业模式，根据客户需求（如降低柴油成本、保障不间断供电）提供高性价比的技术与商务方案。 项目交付保障： 与技术及工程团队紧密协作，确保项目顺利并网、交付及后期运维保障。 4. 品牌建设与市场分析 品牌占位： 代表公司参与当地行业协会（如AMDA）、能源峰会及展会（如摩洛哥EVS展），提升星星充电在当地的品牌声誉。 竞品监控： 持续调研当地政策法规、电网标准及竞争对手动态（如法国EDF、本地集成商），定期输出市场分析报告。 5. 团队搭建与管理 本土化团队建设： 负责本地核心团队的组建、培养与日常管理，打造一支具备战斗力的“中方+本地”混血团队，传承公司文化。 【任职资格】 学历经验： 本科及以上学历，电气工程、电力系统、能源经济等相关专业优先。5年以上新能源（储能、光伏、微电网）项目开发与落地经验，具备中资企业驻外经历者优先。 属地化知识： 深刻理解非洲目标国家的投资环境、劳工法、税务政策及电力行业准入规则，能够处理复杂的清关、运输及签证问题。 专业能力： 具备扎实的电力系统知识，能向客户清晰讲解“光储充”一体化及微电网技术原理与商业价值。 商业与金融思维： 具备优秀的财务分析能力，能够独立测算项目IRR，并利用金融工具（如PPA、融资租赁）解决非洲市场支付能力痛点。 语言与软技能： 精通英语或法语（视国家而定），可作为工作语言进行技术与商务谈判。 具备极强的抗压能力、商业敏锐度及跨文化沟通能力。 地点： 接受长期在非洲工作（每年至少10个月以上常驻）。 【加分项】 拥有当地政府、大型矿业集团或电力公司高层人脉资源。 熟悉华为、阳光电源、德业、固德威等同行的非洲业务运作模式。 具备从0到1的办事处/分公司筹建经验。

Oversees system configuration and process improvements in EMS in collaboration with Event Services. Manages upkeep and posting of schedules to the Final Exam Information SharePoint. Processes section time change workflow requests ensuring alternative room assignments are available in EMS. Works closely with campus partners in University Facilities and Instructional Media Services to resolve facilities and technology issues impacting the centrally scheduled classroom pool. Produces advanced utilization reports and presentations for the Office of the Provost, Facilities, and senior leadership. Works with the University Registrar, the Senior Associate Registrar for Academic Services, and the Office of the Provost to address complex scheduling challenges and develop long-term strategies. Plans accordingly for future goals and objectives as defined by the division of Enrollment Management and Student Success (EMSS) and the University’s strategic plan in association to scheduling, student services, and new building/classroom creation. Supervises the Exammail email account and responds to all section room change requests. Provides clear, visually engaging, and structured documentation for academic departments regarding room scheduling, university time blocks, course distribution policy, etc. Contributes to annual scheduling activities, including First-Year Block Registration and annual course audit processes (July operations may require evening work.) Provides operational continuity during emergencies and strategic initiatives led by senior leadership.
